//: Index plan. Deploy with: firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes
//fieldOverrides: Firestore auto-creates single-field indexes at COLLECTION scope ONLY. A collectionGroup query (allDescendants:true) filtering or ordering on a field needs an explicit COLLECTION_GROUP entry — without it the query fails FAILED_PRECONDITION. An override REPLACES the automatic config, so the default ASCENDING/DESCENDING COLLECTION entries are re-declared here on purpose.

indexes.//: worker/src/routes/invoices.ts — where orgId EQUAL + newest-first. Today the query omits orderBy and takes an arbitrary 1000-doc window sorted in JS (see the DATA-LOSS BUG note there). With this index the query can become orderBy createdAt DESC + limit 50.

worker/src/routes/my-tickets.ts — where uid EQUAL + newest-first. Today orderBy is omitted (no composite index existed) and the caller's tickets are sorted in memory under a 300 cap. With this index: orderBy createdAt DESC + limit 50.

fieldOverrides.//: worker/src/routes/platform-token-usage.ts:80 — collectionGroup 'rollups' WHERE month EQUAL. Missing COLLECTION_GROUP scope => the rollup fast path throws, and the route falls through to a 5000-doc raw usage scan (or 502).

worker/src/routes/platform-metrics.ts:149 — collectionGroup 'tokens' WHERE balance > 0. Missing COLLECTION_GROUP scope => the query throws, is swallowed by the catch, and the token-active-orgs metric silently reports 0.

worker/src/routes/contacts.ts:147 — collectionGroup 'contacts' ORDER BY createdAt DESC. Missing COLLECTION_GROUP scope => the ordered query throws and the code degrades to an unordered re-query sorted in JS (that fallback stays as a safety net).
